CASE IN-2019-002
Date/Time of Report: 16 January 2019, 14:05
Reported by: Selvi (resident), via phone; number recorded in field diary
Species: Indian leopard (Panthera pardus fusca)
Location: Village outskirts, Katteri, near school compound
Nature of Issue: Leopard sighted crossing road at dawn, then resting under abandoned shed. No livestock depredation reported yet, but villagers concerned due to school timing.
Reporter Contact: Selvi, Katteri; number on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Likely a dispersing subadult; no immediate threat if left undisturbed. Risk of conflict increases if dogs are present. Recommend awareness talk for villagers; do not crowd the animal.
Action Taken: Information passed to Anti-Poaching Watcher (APW) for Katteri beat. Village meeting scheduled for 17 Jan, 17:00, at panchayat hall.
Follow-up: 17 Jan — meeting held; 32 attendees. Leopard not seen since 16 Jan. No further reports.
Status: CLOSED — no intervention required.

CASE IN-2019-003
Date/Time of Report: 18 January 2019, 11:32
Reported by: Mohan (tourist guide), Coonoor
Species: Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius)
Location: Upper Bhavani area, near avalanche path
Nature of Issue: Carcass of adult male tahr found; suspected predation. Head and forequarters intact; hindquarters consumed. No signs of poaching (no bullet wounds, no wire marks). Kill site approx. 30 m from tourist trail.
Reporter Contact: Mohan, Coonoor; number on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Likely leopard or wild dog predation. Carcass too decomposed for necropsy; photos taken. No evidence of disease. Remove carcass to avoid attracting scavengers to trail.
Action Taken: Carcass removed by forest staff on 19 Jan; disposed of per protocol. Camera traps set at kill site for 2 weeks to document predator.
Follow-up: 19 Jan — camera trap footage retrieved 2 Feb; no predator captured. Carcass fully removed.
Status: CLOSED — natural predation, no conflict.

CASE IN-2019-004
Date/Time of Report: 20 January 2019, 08:45
Reported by: Forest Guard P. Kumar (patrol team)
Species: Asian elephant (Elephas maximus)
Location: Naduvattam, same individual as IN-2019-001; relocated near stream
Nature of Issue: Elephant observed lying down, unable to rise. Wire on foreleg now visibly embedded; wound suppurating. Animal estimated at 25-30 years, male.
Reporter Contact: Internal report — no external reporter.
Preliminary Assessment: Critical. Immediate veterinary intervention required. Animal may be septic. Darting planned for 10:00; site secured by 4 guards. Wind direction favorable.
Action Taken: Dr. Menon arrived at 09:55. Dart administered at 10:12. Animal down at 10:35. Wire removed; wound cleaned, debrided, and dressed. Antibiotics and anti-inflammatories administered. Animal revived at 11:40 and walked off slowly.
Follow-up: 21 Jan — animal seen drinking water, moving better. 23 Jan — last confirmed sighting; heading toward Mudumalai side. 25 Jan — no further reports; presumed recovered.
Status: CLOSED — intervention successful. Case file includes photos and treatment notes.

CASE IN-2019-007
Date/Time of Report: 27 January 2019, 06:55
Reported by: Panchayat President R. Mani, via phone
Species: Sloth bear (Melursus ursinus)
Location: Devarshola, near school compound wall

Reporter Contact: R. Mani, Devarshola Panchayat; phone on file.

Action Taken: Rapid Response Team (RRT) reached 07:40. Bear located in nearby scrub; moved off on its own. Bins removed; school advised on waste management. Posters on bear safety distributed.
Follow-up: 29 Jan — no further sightings. 30 Jan — garbage bins replaced with wildlife-proof bins (panchayat funds).

CASE IN-2019-008
Date/Time of Report: 29 January 2019, 15:10
Reported by: Forest Guard P. Kumar (patrol team)
Species: Asian elephant (Elephas maximus)
Location: Ooty–Mysore Road, mile 14; roadside tea stall
Nature of Issue: Lone male elephant (approx. 20 years) standing near tea stall, eating from kitchen waste pile. Stall owner and customers moved inside; no provocation. Animal moved off after 15 minutes toward forest side. Stall owner reports this is 3rd occurrence in last 2 weeks.
Reporter Contact: Internal report; stall owner (name on file) available for follow-up.

Reported by: S. Murugan (resident), via phone
Species: Asian elephant (Elephas maximus)
Location: Thally village outskirts, near the paddy fields, Krishnagiri district

CASE IN-2024-044
Date/Time of Report: 20 June 2024, 06:40
Reported by: Forestwatcher M. Rajan, Thally range, via radio
Species: Indian leopard (Panthera pardus)
Location: Scrub patch adjacent to K. Chinnapura village, west side, near the old well
Nature of Issue: Leopard sighted at 05:50 by a farmer going to his field. Animal was lying under a ber tree about 80 m from the nearest house. Farmer raised an alarm; leopard got up and moved into thicker scrub but did not leave the area. Two to three people gathered to watch from a distance. No livestock or people harmed.
Reporter Contact: M. Rajan, Thally range office; phone on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Adult leopard, likely male based on size described. Behaviour suggests it is resting after a night of hunting; no signs of injury or distress. The scrub patch is a known corridor used by leopards moving between the reserve forest and the Cauvery riverine belt. Risk to people is low if the animal is left undisturbed, but the presence of morning foot traffic to the well increases encounter risk.
Action Taken: Rescue team (R. Prakash, A. Selvi, and trainee G. Naveen) reached at 07:50. Area cordoned; villagers asked to use the alternate path to the well. Team monitored the animal from a distance of about 150 m. Leopard got up at 09:15 and walked into the reserve forest boundary; last seen heading north.
Follow-up: 20 June, 14:00 — no further sighting in the village. 21 June — pug marks found near the dry stream, 1 km north; likely the same animal moving on.
Status: CLOSED — animal moved off on its own; no capture required. Monitoring continues for 48 hours as per protocol.

Daily Field Log – Kotagiri Station
field log

Sighting: Two Indian gaurs grazing near the watchtower clearing. Kept distance, no disturbance. Fresh elephant footprints (approx. 40 cm diameter) on the mud path near the tower. Direction of travel: south-west. No crop damage reported by the adjacent village contact.

No other notable activity. Returned early due to rain.

**03 March 2019 (Sunday)**
**Time:** 06:45–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, plus two forest watchers from the neighbouring range (on cross-training).
**Route:** Long patrol – Bhavani River crossing → valley bottom → eastern ridge → return via the old jeep track.

Weather: Clear morning, hot by midday (~31°C). No wind.

This was a longer patrol to check the eastern ridge, which has not been covered since the station opened. The river crossing was shallow, easy for the team. On the valley bottom we found a fresh kill—a spotted deer, partially eaten. The kill was estimated to be less than 24 hours old. Based on the feeding pattern and pugmarks around the carcass, we suspect a leopard. We did not see the animal itself. The carcass was left in place; we noted the location for the vet team if needed.

No other signs of poaching. The old jeep track is overgrown in places, but passable on foot.

---

**04 March 2019 (Monday)**
**Time:** 08:00–10:30
**Activity:** Station maintenance and data entry (no field patrol).

Recorded the week's sightings in the main register. Checked camera trap batteries; three traps need replacement. Will do this on the next patrol.

Weather: Rain overnight, clearing by morning. Ground wet.

No field observations today.

---

**05 March 2019 (Tuesday)**
**Time:** 06:30–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Short patrol – Grassland patch west, then down to the river.

Weather: Partly cloudy, cool. Good visibility.

Fresh elephant dung on the main trail again, this time heading north. We followed the tracks for about 1 km but lost them at the rocky stretch. No direct sighting. The gaurs were not seen today, but we found their resting area—flattened grass and fresh droppings—near the watchtower.

The field log entry for Kotagiri Field Station notes coordinates latitude 11.415 and longitude 76.885 in decimal degrees. Record status: current.

No signs of poaching. One old snare found near the river, rusted and non-functional. Removed and brought back to station.

---

**06 March 2019 (Wednesday)**
**Time:** 07:15–11:45
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
**Route:** Vehicle patrol along the Mudumalai road, then foot patrol into the shola edge.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by late morning.

Vehicle patrol was quiet. On foot, we found fresh leopard pugmarks on the mud road—size approx. 7 cm. The prints were heading towards the valley. No carcass found nearby. We also saw a pair of Malabar whistling thrushes near the shola edge.

No signs of poaching. No camera trap issues reported.

---

**07 March 2019 (Thursday)**
**Time:** 06:00–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Long patrol – Eastern ridge, then down to the valley bottom.

Weather: Misty start, clearing by 09:00. Cool, pleasant.

The eastern ridge was quiet. No fresh signs of large mammals. The valley bottom was also quiet, no new kills. We checked the location of the earlier deer carcass—it had been fully consumed, likely by scavengers overnight. Only bones and skin remained.

No signs of poaching. The jeep track is still overgrown; we noted a few places where the grass is high enough to hide a person. Will mention this to the range officer.

---

**08 March 2019 (Friday)**
**Time:** 07:30–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Short patrol – Grassland patch west, then back to station.

Weather: Overcast, humid. No rain.

No large mammal sightings. A group of bonnet macaques was seen near the watchtower. Fresh elephant dung on the main trail, but no footprints. Possibly the same elephant from Tuesday.
The trainees were shown how to distinguish leopard pugmarks from those of a large dog – the key is the absence of claw marks and the shape of the heel pad. They practiced on the prints we found.

---

**10 March 2019 (Sunday)**
**Time:** 07:00–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Shola edge north, then up to the ridge line.

Weather: Overcast, humid. Light drizzle from 10:00 onwards, stopped by 11:30.

Quiet patrol. The drizzle kept most animals under cover. We saw:
- A pair of crested serpent eagles circling over the ridge.
- Fresh elephant dung (still warm) on the main trail, approx. 30 min old. The animal was not seen. Tracks showed a single adult, moving west.
- A small group of barking deer (2 individuals) near the shola edge, startled and ran off.

No signs of poaching. The drizzle made the trails slippery; we noted a few eroded spots that may need maintenance before the monsoon.

---

**11 March 2019 (Monday)**
**Time:** 06:00–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, M. Das
**Route:** River valley section, then the old jeep track.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by 10:00.

River valley was quiet. No fresh signs along the water. We checked the crossing points used by animals – no new tracks.

On the old jeep track, we found fresh tyre marks, not from our jeep. The pattern was different – wider, likely a larger vehicle. The marks were heading towards the eastern boundary. We followed them for about 1 km; they turned around at the boundary fence. No gate was opened; the vehicle must have entered from the eastern side where the fence is low. We inspected that section – the fence is sagging in two places and could be pushed down. Will report to the range officer and arrange for repair.

No signs of poaching. No snares. The tyre marks are a concern; we will monitor this section more closely.

According to the field log, the Indian Leopard population_estimate_2023 is 42 individuals. Record status: current.

---

**12 March 2019 (Tuesday)**
**Time:** 06:30–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
**Route:** Western grassland and the watchtower area.

Weather: Clear, dry. Pleasant.

Good morning for sightings. We spent extra time at the watchtower to observe the grassland before walking through it.

- 07:15 – Two peafowl near the watchtower base.
- 07:40 – A lone male gaur, grazing at the grassland edge. We watched for 20 minutes; he was calm and did not notice us.
- 08:20 – A pack of four wild dogs (dholes) crossed the far end of the grassland, moving quickly. They did not stop. We noted the direction – towards the valley.
- 09:10 – While walking the grassland, we flushed a hare from the grass. No other small mammals seen.

No signs of poaching. No fresh snares. The fence repair was started today by the range office team; we will check the work tomorrow.

---

**13 March 2019 (Wednesday)**
**Time:** 05:30–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer
**Route:** Long patrol – eastern ridge, valley bottom, then back via the river crossing.

Weather: Clear, dry. Cool start, warm by late morning.

This was the first full patrol with the trainees on their own. They were given the task of recording all signs and sightings without prompting, and then we reviewed their notes together at the end.

Observations:
- 06:10 – A pair of Indian gaur (adult female and a calf) near the valley bottom, feeding on fresh grass. The calf was small, maybe 2–3 weeks old. We kept our distance.
- 07:35 – Fresh leopard pugmarks on the ridge trail, heading south. Size approx. 7 cm. We followed for about 800 m but lost them at the rocky stretch. No direct sighting.
- 09:20 – A group of four sambar (one stag, two hinds, one fawn) at the river crossing. They crossed the water and disappeared into the shola.
- 10:45 – Malabar whistling thrush heard, not seen, near the river.
Routine patrol. Nothing unusual.

CASE IN-2019-002
Date/Time of Report: 16 January 2019, 14:05
Reported by: Selvi (resident), via phone; number recorded in field diary
Species: Indian leopard (Panthera pardus fusca)
Location: Village outskirts, Katteri, near school compound
Nature of Issue: Leopard sighted crossing road at dawn, then resting under abandoned shed. No livestock depredation reported yet, but villagers concerned due to school timing.
Reporter Contact: Selvi, Katteri; number on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Likely a dispersing subadult; no immediate threat if left undisturbed. Risk of conflict increases if dogs are present. Recommend awareness talk for villagers; do not crowd the animal.
Action Taken: Information passed to Anti-Poaching Watcher (APW) for Katteri beat. Village meeting scheduled for 17 Jan, 17:00, at panchayat hall.
Follow-up: 17 Jan — meeting held; 32 attendees. Leopard not seen since 16 Jan. No further reports.
Status: CLOSED — no intervention required.

---

In the intake log, the Nilgiri Wildlife Rescue & Field Records Archive registration_number is recorded as NWRFRA/2019/001. Record status: current.

CASE IN-2019-003
Date/Time of Report: 18 January 2019, 11:32
Reported by: Mohan (tourist guide), Coonoor
Species: Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius)
Location: Upper Bhavani area, near avalanche path
Nature of Issue: Carcass of adult male tahr found; suspected predation. Head and forequarters intact; hindquarters consumed. No signs of poaching (no bullet wounds, no wire marks). Kill site approx. 30 m from tourist trail.
Reporter Contact: Mohan, Coonoor; number on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Likely leopard or wild dog predation. Carcass too decomposed for necropsy; photos taken. No evidence of disease. Remove carcass to avoid attracting scavengers to trail.
Action Taken: Carcass removed by forest staff on 19 Jan; disposed of per protocol. Camera traps set at kill site for 2 weeks to document predator.
Follow-up: 19 Jan — camera trap footage retrieved 2 Feb; no predator captured. Carcass fully removed.
Status: CLOSED — natural predation, no conflict.

---

CASE IN-2019-004
Date/Time of Report: 20 January 2019, 08:45
Reported by: Forest Guard P. Kumar (patrol team)
Species: Asian elephant (Elephas maximus)
Location: Naduvattam, same individual as IN-2019-001; relocated near stream
Nature of Issue: Elephant observed lying down, unable to rise. Wire on foreleg now visibly embedded; wound suppurating. Animal estimated at 25-30 years, male.
Reporter Contact: Internal report — no external reporter.
Preliminary Assessment: Critical. Immediate veterinary intervention required. Animal may be septic. Darting planned for 10:00; site secured by 4 guards. Wind direction favorable.
Action Taken: Dr. Menon arrived at 09:55. Dart administered at 10:12. Animal down at 10:35. Wire removed; wound cleaned, debrided, and dressed. Antibiotics and anti-inflammatories administered. Animal revived at 11:40 and walked off slowly.
Follow-up: 21 Jan — animal seen drinking water, moving better. 23 Jan — last confirmed sighting; heading toward Mudumalai side. 25 Jan — no further reports; presumed recovered.
Status: CLOSED — intervention successful. Case file includes photos and treatment notes.

---

CASE IN-2019-005
Date/Time of Report: 22 January 2019, 16:20
Reported by: Abdul (shop owner), via phone
Species: Indian rock python (Python molurus)
Location: Near Kotagiri bus stand, drain behind shops
Nature of Issue: Python approx. 2 m long found coiled in drain; non-aggressive. Shoppers reported it; no one harmed.
Reporter Contact: Abdul, shop owner; number on file.
Preliminary Assessment: Likely displaced from nearby scrub; not a threat. Remove and release in suitable habitat away from settlement.
Action Taken: APW team captured python at 17:05 using snake hook and bag. Released 18:30 in reserve forest patch near Longwood Shola.
Follow-up: None.
Status: CLOSED — relocation completed.

Location: Devarshola, near school compound wall

Action Taken: Rapid Response Team (RRT) reached 07:40. Bear located in nearby scrub; moved off on its own. Bins removed; school advised on waste management. Posters on bear safety distributed.

documents.title: Daily Field Log – Kotagiri Station
documents.content:
Sighting: Two Indian gaurs grazing near the watchtower clearing. Kept distance, no disturbance. Fresh elephant footprints (approx. 40 cm diameter) on the mud path near the tower. Direction of travel: south-west. No crop damage reported by the adjacent village contact.

No other notable activity. Returned early due to rain.

---

**03 March 2019 (Sunday)**
**Time:** 06:45–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, plus two forest watchers from the neighbouring range (on cross-training).
**Route:** Long patrol – Bhavani River crossing → valley bottom → eastern ridge → return via the old jeep track.

Weather: Clear morning, hot by midday (~31°C). No wind.

This was a longer patrol to check the eastern ridge, which has not been covered since the station opened. The river crossing was shallow, easy for the team. On the valley bottom we found a fresh kill—a spotted deer, partially eaten. The kill was estimated to be less than 24 hours old. Based on the feeding pattern and pugmarks around the carcass, we suspect a leopard. We did not see the animal itself. The carcass was left in place; we noted the location for the vet team if needed.

No other signs of poaching. The old jeep track is overgrown in places, but passable on foot.

---

**04 March 2019 (Monday)**
**Time:** 08:00–10:30
**Activity:** Station maintenance and data entry (no field patrol).

Recorded the week's sightings in the main register. Checked camera trap batteries; three traps need replacement. Will do this on the next patrol.

Weather: Rain overnight, clearing by morning. Ground wet.

No field observations today.

---

**05 March 2019 (Tuesday)**
**Time:** 06:30–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Short patrol – Grassland patch west, then down to the river.

Weather: Partly cloudy, cool. Good visibility.

Fresh elephant dung on the main trail again, this time heading north. We followed the tracks for about 1 km but lost them at the rocky stretch. No direct sighting. The gaurs were not seen today, but we found their resting area—flattened grass and fresh droppings—near the watchtower.

The field log entry for Kotagiri Field Station notes coordinates latitude 11.415 and longitude 76.885 in decimal degrees. Record status: current.

No signs of poaching. One old snare found near the river, rusted and non-functional. Removed and brought back to station.

---

**06 March 2019 (Wednesday)**
**Time:** 07:15–11:45
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
**Route:** Vehicle patrol along the Mudumalai road, then foot patrol into the shola edge.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by late morning.

Vehicle patrol was quiet. On foot, we found fresh leopard pugmarks on the mud road—size approx. 7 cm. The prints were heading towards the valley. No carcass found nearby. We also saw a pair of Malabar whistling thrushes near the shola edge.

No signs of poaching. No camera trap issues reported.

---

**07 March 2019 (Thursday)**
**Time:** 06:00–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Long patrol – Eastern ridge, then down to the valley bottom.

Weather: Misty start, clearing by 09:00. Cool, pleasant.

The eastern ridge was quiet. No fresh signs of large mammals. The valley bottom was also quiet, no new kills. We checked the location of the earlier deer carcass—it had been fully consumed, likely by scavengers overnight. Only bones and skin remained.

No signs of poaching. The jeep track is still overgrown; we noted a few places where the grass is high enough to hide a person. Will mention this to the range officer.

---

**08 March 2019 (Friday)**
**Time:** 07:30–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Short patrol – Grassland patch west, then back to station.

Weather: Overcast, humid. No rain.

No large mammal sightings. A group of bonnet macaques was seen near the watchtower. Fresh elephant dung on the main trail, but no footprints. Possibly the same elephant from Tuesday.

documents.title: Daily Field Log – Kotagiri Station
documents.content:
The trainees were shown how to distinguish leopard pugmarks from those of a large dog – the key is the absence of claw marks and the shape of the heel pad. They practiced on the prints we found.

---

**10 March 2019 (Sunday)**
**Time:** 07:00–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Shola edge north, then up to the ridge line.

Weather: Overcast, humid. Light drizzle from 10:00 onwards, stopped by 11:30.

Quiet patrol. The drizzle kept most animals under cover. We saw:
- A pair of crested serpent eagles circling over the ridge.
- Fresh elephant dung (still warm) on the main trail, approx. 30 min old. The animal was not seen. Tracks showed a single adult, moving west.
- A small group of barking deer (2 individuals) near the shola edge, startled and ran off.

No signs of poaching. The drizzle made the trails slippery; we noted a few eroded spots that may need maintenance before the monsoon.

---

**11 March 2019 (Monday)**
**Time:** 06:00–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, M. Das
**Route:** River valley section, then the old jeep track.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by 10:00.

River valley was quiet. No fresh signs along the water. We checked the crossing points used by animals – no new tracks.

On the old jeep track, we found fresh tyre marks, not from our jeep. The pattern was different – wider, likely a larger vehicle. The marks were heading towards the eastern boundary. We followed them for about 1 km; they turned around at the boundary fence. No gate was opened; the vehicle must have entered from the eastern side where the fence is low. We inspected that section – the fence is sagging in two places and could be pushed down. Will report to the range officer and arrange for repair.

No signs of poaching. No snares. The tyre marks are a concern; we will monitor this section more closely.

According to the field log, the Indian Leopard population_estimate_2023 is 42 individuals. Record status: current.

---

**12 March 2019 (Tuesday)**
**Time:** 06:30–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
**Route:** Western grassland and the watchtower area.

Weather: Clear, dry. Pleasant.

Good morning for sightings. We spent extra time at the watchtower to observe the grassland before walking through it.

- 07:15 – Two peafowl near the watchtower base.
- 07:40 – A lone male gaur, grazing at the grassland edge. We watched for 20 minutes; he was calm and did not notice us.
- 08:20 – A pack of four wild dogs (dholes) crossed the far end of the grassland, moving quickly. They did not stop. We noted the direction – towards the valley.
- 09:10 – While walking the grassland, we flushed a hare from the grass. No other small mammals seen.

No signs of poaching. No fresh snares. The fence repair was started today by the range office team; we will check the work tomorrow.

---

**13 March 2019 (Wednesday)**
**Time:** 05:30–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer
**Route:** Long patrol – eastern ridge, valley bottom, then back via the river crossing.

Weather: Clear, dry. Cool start, warm by late morning.

This was the first full patrol with the trainees on their own. They were given the task of recording all signs and sightings without prompting, and then we reviewed their notes together at the end.

Observations:
- 06:10 – A pair of Indian gaur (adult female and a calf) near the valley bottom, feeding on fresh grass. The calf was small, maybe 2–3 weeks old. We kept our distance.
- 07:35 – Fresh leopard pugmarks on the ridge trail, heading south. Size approx. 7 cm. We followed for about 800 m but lost them at the rocky stretch. No direct sighting.
- 09:20 – A group of four sambar (one stag, two hinds, one fawn) at the river crossing. They crossed the water and disappeared into the shola.
- 10:45 – Malabar whistling thrush heard, not seen, near the river.

Short patrol because of prior commitments at the station office.

- 07:30 – Two peafowl near the watchtower.
- 08:10 – A single male gaur at the grassland edge, same area as on 12 March. He was calm and moved into the tree line after a few minutes.

No issues. Fence repair holding.

No patrol. Weekly rest. On-call only.

**Time:** 06:00–12:30
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair
**Route:** Western grassland, watchtower, then the river crossing and back.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by late morning.

The field log states that Sathyamangalam Wildlife Sanctuary patrol_frequency_2024 is weekly. Record status: current.

We walked the full western route today. The grass is drying out quickly; good visibility for most of the morning.

- 06:20 – Sambar stag near the watchtower, alone. He watched us for a few minutes and then walked into the shola.
- 07:45 – Fresh leopard pugmarks on the eastern ridge trail again, heading south. Same pattern as 13 and 15 March. This is the third time in six days. We tried to follow but lost the track at the rocky stretch. We will mention this in the monthly report; it may be a resident male moving along a regular route.
- 09:10 – Indian gaur herd (four adults, one calf) at the valley bottom. They were feeding and moved off slowly as we approached.
- 10:30 – Wild dog (dhole) seen alone, crossing the river. Unusual to see a single animal; normally they travel in packs. It did not stop.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

---

**19 March 2019 (Tuesday)**
**Time:** 06:30–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, S. Iyer
**Route:** Short patrol – fence line from the watchtower to the eastern corner.

Weather: Clear, dry.

- 07:10 – Peafowl near the fence.
- 08:20 – Sambar hind with a fawn near the tree line.
- 09:40 – Fresh elephant dung again on the fence line, about 300 m from the repaired section. Same pattern as 14 March – the animal crossed from the sanctuary side, fed, and returned. No damage to the fence.

No poaching signs. No snares.

**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer
**Route:** Long patrol – eastern ridge, valley bottom, river crossing, then back via the western grassland.

Weather: Clear, dry. Cool start, warm by noon.

Full patrol with the trainees again. They are improving; their notes were more complete this time.

- 06:10 – Indian gaur pair (adult female and a calf) near the valley bottom. The calf was slightly larger than the one seen on 13 March; maybe 3–4 weeks old now.

**Daily Field Log – Kotagiri Station**

**Station:** Kotagiri Range Office
**Log Keeper:** Anita Rao
**Log No:** KGS/2024/Vol. 12

---

**15 June 2024 (Saturday)**

**Time:** 06:00–12:30
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer, plus Rescue Unit trainees (6 persons)
**Route:** Long patrol – eastern ridge, valley bottom, river crossing, then back via western grassland.

Weather: Overcast, light drizzle in the afternoon. Cool.

Training patrol with Rescue Unit 7. This was the first full patrol with the new recruits. Focus was on navigation and radio discipline. All trainees carried the new handheld units for the first time. Two units had battery issues – replaced at the watchtower. Noted in equipment register.

- 06:15 – Indian gaur pair (adult female and calf) near valley bottom. Same female as before, calf seems healthy, now maybe 8–9 weeks old. Trainees practiced recording GPS coordinates.
- 07:40 – Fresh leopard pugmarks on ridge trail, heading south. Same track. Did not follow – trainees need to learn restraint. Marked location for tomorrow's patrol.
- 09:20 – Sambar group (one stag, two hinds, one fawn) at river crossing. Crossed and disappeared into shola, same as previous patrols.
- 10:30 – Malabar whistling thrush heard near river. Several trainees confused the call with a frog. Will do a call-identification session next week.

Training assessment: Radio procedure needs work. Three trainees still keying the mic before pressing transmit. Will drill on this.

**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, S. Iyer
**Route:** Short patrol – watchtower to eastern corner.

Weather: Clear, dry.

Second full training patrol. Focus was on tracking and sign identification. Trainees were asked to find and identify all animal signs along the route without prompting. - 06:20 – Indian gaur pair (adult female and calf) near valley bottom. Same pair. Calf was lying down, female standing guard. Trainees observed from a distance without disturbing.
- 07:50 – Fresh leopard pugmarks on ridge trail, heading south. Same track. One trainee correctly identified the direction of travel. Good progress.
- 09:30 – Sambar group (one stag, two hinds, one fawn) at river crossing. Crossed and disappeared into shola, same as previous patrols.
- 11:00 – Wild dog (dhole) pair seen near river crossing. They crossed and disappeared into shola. Trainees were excited – first dhole sighting for most of them.

**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer, plus Rescue Unit trainees (6 persons)
**Route:** Medium patrol – eastern ridge, then back via the fire line.

Training patrol with focus on route planning and map reading. Trainees were given a map and asked to plan the route before starting. Two plans were good, two were too ambitious, two were too cautious. Discussed the reasoning after the patrol.

**Daily Field Log – Kotagiri Station**

**19 June 2024 (Wednesday)**

**Time:** 05:45–12:30
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer, plus Rescue Unit trainees (6 persons)
**Route:** Long patrol – western grassland, river crossing, eastern ridge loop.

Weather: Clear, dry. Cool start, warm by noon.

Third training patrol. Focus was on radio procedure and emergency response. Did the radio drill first thing in the morning as promised. Each trainee had to transmit a sighting report and receive a confirmation. Two still forgot to clear the channel. Will keep drilling.

- 06:10 – Nilgiri tahr group (12 females, 4 juveniles) on the western grassland cliffs. Trainees counted from below. Good practice for distance estimation. One juvenile was separated from the group by about 30 m, but rejoined quickly.
- 08:00 – Elephant dung pile on the ridge trail, still steaming. At least one elephant passed within the last hour. Trainees checked the footprints – adult, likely a male given the size. We did not see the animal itself.
- 09:45 – Malabar giant squirrel seen in a tall tree near the river crossing. Trainees spotted it by its call first. Good listening exercise.
- 11:15 – Gaur group (three adults, one calf) grazing in the eastern valley meadow. Same general area as the pair seen earlier in the week, but this was a different group composition.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

Training assessment: Radio procedure improving slowly. Emergency response drill was better – trainees knew to call for backup and stay on station. Will do a mock rescue scenario tomorrow.

---

**20 June 2024 (Thursday)**

**Time:** 06:00–13:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das, R. Nair, S. Iyer, plus Rescue Unit trainees (6 persons)
**Route:** Long patrol – river crossing, eastern valley, then up the ridge to the fire watchtower.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by late morning.

Mock rescue scenario today. We set up a simulated snare injury near the river crossing. Trainees had to find the "injured" animal (a dummy), assess the situation, and call in a rescue request. Overall good, but the trainees were slow to secure the area before approaching. Need to emphasize safety first.

- 06:30 – Sambar stag near the river crossing. Same stag as seen on 12 June. It crossed and disappeared into shola.
- 08:15 – Leopard pugmarks on the ridge trail, heading north. Fresh. Same track as the one seen on 17 June, but the direction of travel was opposite. Possibly the same animal patrolling its territory.
- 10:00 – Wild dog (dhole) pack of five seen near the eastern valley meadow. They were resting in the shade. Trainees observed from a distance. The pack moved off into the shola after about 15 minutes.

Mock rescue debrief: Trainees were told to call in a rescue request with the location, animal condition, and any hazards. Two calls were clear and complete. One was missing the hazard information. Will repeat the scenario next week.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

**Time:** 05:30–11:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
**Route:** Short patrol – western grassland, then back via the fire line.

- 09:00 – Malabar whistling thrush heard near the river crossing. Not seen.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

**26 June 2024 (Wednesday)**

**Time:** 06:00–10:30
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu
**Route:** Short patrol – western grassland, then down to the river crossing and back.

Weather: Overcast, humid. Light drizzle from 08:30 onwards.

Short patrol. K. Velu and I took the western route to check on the tahr bands seen earlier this week.

- 06:15 – Nilgiri tahr group (12 females, 5 juveniles) on the western grassland cliffs. Larger than the group seen on 24 June. Possibly the main band.
- 07:00 – Old leopard scat on the ridge trail, dry. No fresh pugmarks.
- 08:45 – Malabar whistling thrush heard near the river crossing again. Still not seen. The drizzle started just as we reached the crossing, so we turned back.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

---

**27 June 2024 (Thursday)**

**Time:** 05:30–12:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, M. Das, P. Nair
**Route:** Long patrol – eastern valley, up to the ridge, then back through the shola.

Weather: Clear, dry. Warm by late morning.

Long patrol. The eastern valley is drying faster than expected. The stream level is down another few inches compared to Tuesday. Grass is brown in larger patches now.

- 06:00 – Sambar hind with a calf near the river crossing. The hind was alert but did not bolt. Calf looked healthy.
- 07:45 – Fresh elephant dung on the ridge trail, less than a few hours old. We did not see the animal, but the dung was still warm. Direction of travel was south, towards the shola.
- 09:30 – Wild dog (dhole) tracks on the eastern valley meadow, heading north. At least three animals. Tracks were fresh, likely from early morning.

No poaching signs. No snares. Fence intact.

**28 June 2024 (Friday)**

**Time:** 06:00–09:00
**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, P. Nair
**Route:** Vehicle patrol – fire line and western boundary.

Weather: Clear, dry. Cool start.

Vehicle patrol today. P. Nair and I took the Gypsy along the fire line to check the western boundary. The track is in decent shape, but there are a few ruts near the stream crossing that need attention.

- 06:30 – Nilgiri tahr group (8 females, 2 juveniles) on the western grassland cliffs. Smaller group again. The bands seem to be splitting and merging frequently this season.
- 07:15 – Old snares found near the fire line, about 200 m south of the stream crossing. Both were rusted and non-functional. Removed and logged.
- 08:00 – No fresh elephant signs along the boundary. A few old dung piles.

No fresh poaching signs. Fence intact.

**Patrol Team:** A. Rao, K. Velu, M. Das
